title: Canonical pointed morphism of geometric strict henselizations
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let $X_{(\bar x)}$ and $S_{(f\bar x)}$ be the geometric strict henselizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with structural maps $\rho_{\bar x}$ and $\rho_{f\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Their distinguished $\Omega$-points $i_{\bar x}$ and $i_{f\bar x}$ are the spectra of the canonical point evaluations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-point-evaluation]. The canonical strict-henselization morphism $f_{(\bar x)}:X_{(\bar x)}\to S_{(f\bar x)}$ is the unique pointed morphism over $f$, characterized by $\rho_{f\bar x}\circ f_{(\bar x)}=f\circ\rho_{\bar x}$ and $f_{(\bar x)}\circ i_{\bar x}=i_{f\bar x}$. This specifies the canonical map by its unique defining property, not an arbitrary map or an isomorphism assumption.

source.place: Tags 04HX (strict henselizations at geometric points) and 04GU (functoriality of strict henselizations), as realized by the unique pointed map over the given scheme morphism.
